defects.detail: 'Pharao vidit spicas gen[er]ali' (OCR for Gen. xli citation) rendered as 'Pharaoh saw ears of corn in a general way'
'qui est casus prophetie secundum doctores, est aliquid deficiens a ratione prophetie' collapsed to 'which is a falling short of the definition of prophecy, according to the doctors'
'Motus autem Iepte et consilium [Caiphae]' rendered 'the motion of Jephthah and Caiaphas' (consilium dropped as a term)

reason: Three kinds of prophecy (natural foreknowledge, improper prophecy in vision/speech/operation, true prophecy by degrees) rendered faithfully with Daniel, Caiaphas, Jephthah, Jeremiah, Samuel examples; minor slips on garbled citation 'generali' and the casus/deficiens clause; source OCR heavily abbreviated so confidence moderate.

defects.detail: 'l. senatus de don. cau. ff.' (D. 39.6, mortis causa) and 'l. hoc iure §. fi. ff. de donat.' both converted to 'Digest 39.5.1', as is 'l. Aristo ff. de don.' — three different laws given one modern number
'l. j. ff. de codic. ex leg.' (condictio ex lege, first law) rendered 'Digest 28.2.29'
'in d. §. fi. l. si quis argentum' (final section) rendered 'in the said section 5 of the law Si quis argentum'

reason: Momus's lunar satire on the Doctors and the argument that donation is an innominate contract are rendered faithfully throughout; the translator replaced the medieval legal allegations with modern Digest/Code numbers, several of which do not match the laws cited (l. senatus, l. hoc iure, l. j. de cond. ex lege, §. fi.).
